questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION ONE
questions.question:
The Industrial Revolution that began in England changed how the people worked.

a. Analyze three conditions needed for industrialization (3 Marks)

b. Explain two factors why Britain became the leading manufacturing nation (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any three conditions needed for industrialization:
   1. Raw materials (e.g. coal and iron ore) to feed the factories
   2. Capital (money) to build factories and buy machines
   3. Labour and technology (inventions and machines), a market for the goods, and good transport (roads, canals, railways)

b. Any two factors:
   1. Britain had plenty of coal and iron and a large capital from trade and the colonies
   2. Britain had colonies that supplied raw materials and bought its goods, plus great inventions (steam engine, spinning jenny), a strong navy and political stability

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION TWO
questions.question:
Pan-Africanism is the movement formed at the beginning of the twentieth century by African origin intellectuals.

a. Name any two founding fathers of the Pan-African movement. (2 Marks)

b. Identify three achievements of the Pan-African movement. (3 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any two:
   1. W.E.B. Du Bois
   2. Marcus Garvey (also Henry Sylvester Williams, George Padmore)

b. Any three achievements:
   1. Organised Pan-African congresses that raised world attention to the problems of Africans
   2. Inspired African nationalism and the struggle for independence
   3. Promoted African unity and identity, leading to the formation of the OAU in 1963 (now the African Union)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION FOUR
questions.question:
One of the most important consequences of the First World War was the Russian Revolution of 1917.

a. What reforms did Alexander II make? (2 Marks)

b. Analyze two reasons that the professional government lost power (2 Marks)

c. Define the term communism (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Reforms of Alexander II (any two):
   1. Freed the serfs in 1861 (emancipation)
   2. Introduced judicial, local government (zemstvo), military and education reforms

b. Note: the paper prints 'professional government'; it refers to the Provisional Government that ruled Russia after the Tsar fell in March 1917. Any two reasons it lost power:
   1. It kept Russia in the First World War, which was unpopular and caused more suffering and food shortages
   2. It failed to solve the land question and was weak, sharing power with the Soviets, while the Bolsheviks promised 'peace, land and bread' and seized power in November 1917

c. Communism is a political and economic ideology in which the means of production (land, factories) are owned in common by the community or the state, there is no private property, and the aim is a classless society.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION FIVE
questions.question:
a. Define policy of appeasement (3 Marks)

b. Discuss any two reasons behind the invasion of Japan to Manchuria (4 Marks)

c. List the countries that attended the Munich conference in 1938 (3 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The policy of appeasement was the policy of Britain and France in the 1930s of giving in to the demands of aggressive dictators (Hitler and Mussolini) in order to avoid another war.

b. Any two reasons:
   1. Japan needed raw materials (coal, iron) from Manchuria for its industries
   2. Japan needed land and markets for its growing population and goods, especially after the Great Depression; the army also wanted Manchuria as a strategic buffer against Russia and knew the League of Nations was weak

c. Countries at the Munich conference (1938):
   1. Germany
   2. Britain
   3. France
   4. Italy (Czechoslovakia, the country concerned, was not invited)

a. List three countries that Germany captured at the beginning of the war (3 Marks)

Column B:

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION SEVEN
questions.question:
United Nations organization was created in 1945, after the Second World War.

a. State three achievements of the United Nations Organization (3 Marks)

b. Identify three failures of the United Nations Organization (3 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any three achievements:
   1. Helped to keep peace and settle disputes through peacekeeping missions
   2. Supported decolonization and independence of many countries; adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
   3. Humanitarian and development work through agencies such as UNICEF, WHO, UNESCO and WFP (e.g. fighting disease and hunger)

b. Any three failures:
   1. Failed to prevent some wars and genocides (e.g. Rwanda 1994, Iraq 2003)
   2. The veto power of the five permanent members can block action
   3. It cannot enforce its resolutions without a standing army and depends on the funding and goodwill of powerful states

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION EIGHT
questions.question:
a. Define the term Cold War (3 Marks)

b. Identify the causes of the Cold War (3 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The Cold War was a period of tension, rivalry and hostility (about 1945 to 1991) between the United States and its allies (the capitalist West) and the Soviet Union and its allies (the communist East) that did not become a direct, full-scale war.

b. Any three causes:
   1. Ideological differences: capitalism and democracy (USA) against communism (USSR)
   2. Mistrust between the wartime allies, and the Soviet spread of communism in Eastern Europe
   3. The arms race and the atomic bomb, plus the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan against the Soviet influence

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION NINE
questions.question:
After the downfall of Somalia's central government in January 1991, civil war began.

a. Outline the factors that led to the collapse of the central government (3 Marks)

b. Give Four example of reconciliation conferences after 1991 (4 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any three factors:
   1. The harsh dictatorship and human rights abuses of Siad Barre's regime and clan favouritism
   2. Defeat in the Ogaden War (1977-78) and economic hardship
   3. Armed opposition movements (USC, SNM, SPM, SSDF) and the loss of Cold War support

b. Any four reconciliation conferences:
   1. Arta Conference, Djibouti (2000)
   2. Mbagathi (Nairobi) conference (2002-2004)
   3. Addis Ababa conference (1993)
   4. Sodere (1997) / Cairo (1997) (the Djibouti conferences of 1991-92 are also accepted)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 MARKS) - QUESTION TEN
questions.question:
a. Discuss three common problems to African states after independence (3 Marks)

b. State the achievements of Kwame Nkrumah in Ghana (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any three problems:
   1. Political instability: military coups and one-party dictatorships
   2. Ethnic / tribal conflicts and border disputes
   3. Poverty, poor infrastructure, illiteracy and disease, with continued economic dependence on the former colonial powers (neo-colonialism) and corruption

b. Any two achievements of Kwame Nkrumah:
   1. Led Ghana to independence in 1957 (the first black African colony to gain independence)
   2. Built schools, hospitals, roads, the Tema harbour and the Akosombo dam, and promoted Pan-Africanism (helped found the OAU)

questions.section: PART THREE: EXTENDED QUESTIONS (20 MARKS) - Answer any TWO of the following questions - QUESTION ONE
questions.question:
The Creation of Israel in 1948 led Arab-Israel Wars

a. What did the Zionists believe? (2 Marks)

b. State two factors that caused the Suez war (4 Marks)

c. Identify two results of the Suez war (4 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The Zionists believed that the Jews, as a people, should return to Palestine (their ancient homeland) and set up a Jewish state there.

b. Any two factors:
   1. Egypt's president Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956
   2. Britain and the USA withdrew their offer to fund the Aswan Dam; Egypt also blocked Israeli ships, and Britain, France and Israel wanted to regain control of the canal

c. Any two results:
   1. Britain, France and Israel withdrew under pressure from the UN, USA and USSR, and Egypt kept control of the canal
   2. Nasser's prestige rose in the Arab world; British and French influence declined and Soviet influence increased; UN peacekeepers were stationed in Sinai

questions.section: PART THREE: EXTENDED QUESTIONS (20 MARKS) - Answer any TWO of the following questions - QUESTION TWO
questions.question:
a. State three reasons that motivated Iraq to invade Kuwait (6 Marks)

b. Explain two results of the Gulf war (4 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any three reasons:
   1. Iraq owed huge debts to Kuwait and others after the Iran-Iraq war and wanted them cancelled
   2. Dispute over oil: Kuwait overproduced oil, lowering prices, and was accused of stealing oil from the Rumaila field by slant drilling
   3. Iraq claimed Kuwait as historically part of Iraq, and wanted its oil wealth and better access to the Gulf

b. Any two results:
   1. Iraq was defeated by the US-led coalition and forced out of Kuwait (1991)
   2. UN sanctions were imposed on Iraq, its economy and army were damaged, and oil wells were burned causing environmental damage; US military presence in the Gulf increased

questions.section: PART THREE: EXTENDED QUESTIONS (20 MARKS) - Answer any TWO of the following questions - QUESTION THREE
questions.question:
c. Define Pan-Somalism (4 Marks)

d. Identify three challenges faced the union of British and Italian Somaliland (6 Marks)

(Note: the parts of this question are lettered c and d in the paper.)
questions.answer_guide:
c. Pan-Somalism is the movement and ideology that aimed to unite all Somali-inhabited territories into one Somali state: British Somaliland, Italian Somaliland, French Somaliland (Djibouti), the Ogaden (Ethiopia) and the Northern Frontier District (Kenya), symbolised by the five-pointed star on the Somali flag.

d. Any three challenges:
   1. Different colonial legacies: different administrative, legal (English common law vs Italian law) and education systems
   2. Language differences (English in the north, Italian in the south) and different currencies
   3. Unequal sharing of power and resources: the north felt marginalised because the capital and most government posts were in the south, and many in the north were unhappy with the 1961 constitution

questions.section: PART THREE: EXTENDED QUESTIONS (20 MARKS) - Answer any TWO of the following questions - QUESTION FOUR
questions.question:
a. Explain two political results of the Second World War (6 Marks)

b. Discuss three social results of the Second World War (4 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any two political results:
   1. The USA and the USSR emerged as the two superpowers, leading to the Cold War
   2. The United Nations was formed to keep peace; Germany was divided; colonial powers weakened, which led to the independence of many colonies (decolonisation)

b. Any three social results:
   1. Millions of people were killed (including the Holocaust)
   2. Millions became refugees, homeless and orphans
   3. Cities, homes, schools and hospitals were destroyed, and women took a greater role in work and society
